About this application

This application shows information about 30 different programming languages, including a brief summary of each language\'s history and functionality, and a sample program written in the language. Tap one of the cards to view information about that language.

The programs featured have been tested with a variety of compilers, including those on the website JDoodle (https://www.jdoodle.com). Please note that some of these programs may not work depending on the language version or software you are using.

C was introduced in the early 1970s and developed by Dennis Ritchie at Bell Labs. The programming language has been used in a wide variety of applications, including operating systems and graphical user interfaces, and can grant the user access to memory locations in the computer.

C++ was introduced in 1985. An extension of C, it is mainly known for implementing object-orientated programming with classes, and is the basis of many applications, including compilers used to run scripts from other programming languages.

Java is an object-oriented language released in 1995. Java applications run via a Java virtual machine installed on a host device, meaning the programmer can write an application once and run it on multiple devices without recompiling the application.

Kotlin is a language known for being interoperable with Java, a more concise syntax and features to ensure safe access to variables. It is the preferred language for developing Android applications, superseding Java.

Python was introduced in 1991 and is widely used as an introductory programming language, with a philosophy of user readable code and using indentation to separate blocks of code. Python is an interpreted language, meaning that code is run one line at a time instead of needing to be built and compiled.

JavaScript is used to create interactive content on websites, and alongside HTML and CSS, is a core component of the world wide web. JavaScript code usually runs in the user’s web browser, making it a client end language.

TypeScript is an extension of JavaScript introduced in 2012. Its main feature is the use of static typing to variables, similar to what’s used in languages like Java and C#, making it ideal for more complex projects where variable typing is important.

Haskell is an example of a functional programming language, first introduced in 1990. Variables are stored as the results of functions defined by the user instead of being directly assigned to at runtime, reducing possible side effects at runtime.

C# is a language that was developed by Microsoft staff and became widely available starting in 2000. The language is used throughout Microsoft’s .NET framework, with applications including use in desktop programs and web backends.

Rust is a low-level programming language designed with an emphasis on performance and protected memory. Rust is known for the use of “borrow checking” instead of a typical garbage collector, making applications more lightweight.

Scala is a high-level programming language with support for both object-oriented and functional programming paradigms. Designed to be concise, Scala code can run on top of platforms such as the Java Virtual Machine and JavaScript.

Go is a compiled high level programming language originally developed by staff at Google, with a syntax designed to be simple enough to improve productivity. Go has been adopted by a number of high profile companies, including Microsoft and Dropbox.

Elixir is a functional programming introduced in 2012, emphasising features like lightweight, scalable code and fault tolerance. Running on top of the Erlang virtual machine, Elixir code can be used for a variety of platforms including web development and embedded programs.

BASIC is a family of languages designed to make programming accessible to people in a non-scientific background and was widely used in various home computers from companies like Apple and Commodore. In many BASIC implementations, lines of code begin with a number that can be referenced in later parts of the program.

Ada is an object-orientated language originally used for embedded systems and is known for strong typing and favouring English words over symbols. Named after programmer Ada Lovelace, the language was developed under contract for the United States Department of Defence to replace over 400 languages that were being used.

OCaml is an object-oriented extension of the earlier Caml language, a dialect of the ML language, and supports multiple programming paradigms. OCaml was developed at Inria in France and debuted in 1996, and has influenced future languages like Scala and Rust.

Visual Basic can refer to two languages developed by Microsoft: the original "classic" version based on BASIC, and a successor language that targets the .NET Framework. Both are used in the development of desktop applications with the Windows Forms library. The version featured in this application is the .NET version of the language.

COBOL is a compiled language that was first released in the 1960s, initially supporting procedural and imperative programming. Widely used in business and financial environments, most COBOL programming is dedicated to maintain existing applications, as newer languages are used for more modern applications.
R is a language used mainly for statistical computing. Data represented in R code can be displayed through the use of graphics, including lines, bars and pie charts.

Swift is a general-purpose language that was originally developed for Apple and introduced in 2010. In addition to being used for Apple\'s platforms, the language emphasises scalability, a concise syntax and interoperability with C and C++.

Lua is a high level, interpreted language that debuted in 1993, and is known for being used in embedded systems and scripting video games. As the interpreter is written in C and the language includes a C application programming interface, Lua can run on multiple platforms.

F# is an open-source language that originated as an implementation of the OCaml language for the .NET platform, and is designed primarily as a functional programming language. F# code can also run in JavaScript environments

Objective-C is an object-orientated language based on C, with the addition of message passing inspired by the language Smalltalk. Objective-C was the primarily language used by the company NeXT, and later Apple following NeXT\’s acquisition in 1997.

Ruby is a high-level interpreted language that was developed in the 1990s, with an emphasis on simplicity. Every item in Ruby is treated as an object. Ruby is also the basis of the Ruby on Rails framework, used to develop dynamic websites.

SQL is a language used to create and modify databases and their records, and the language comes in several dialects for various database management systems (DBMS). Code can be saved in the form of a stored procedure, allowing the user to repeatedly make the same query by running the procedure.

PHP is a general-purpose language that focuses on server-side web development. PHP code can be embedded in HTML, and differs from other scripting languages (e.g., JavaScript) by having code run server-side, meaning the end user is unaware of the underlying code that is running.

Bash is a command line shell that runs on Unix and Unix-like operating systems, allowing the user to enter commands to perform a variety of actions. Commands can be saved as a script file, which are automatically performed by shell upon being opened.

Assembly code refers to any low-level code with an instruction set that correspond closely with those of a computer\'s central processing unit (CPU). As CPUs can have different architectures, instruction sets can vary depending on the CPU the code targets (e.g., x86 and ARM are two different CPU architectures and therefore have incompatible instruction sets).

Fortran is a high-level and compiled programming language that was designed at IBM in 1957 and was initially developed as an alternative to using assembly code. Modern uses of Fortran include scientific computing and creating programs to measure the performance of supercomputers.

Elm is a functional language that compiles to JavaScript and is designed for creating graphical user interfaces for web applications. Elm emphasises fast performance and error messages designed to be clearly understood by developers.
